answer: Behavioral ridge fingerprinting ties each agent's model weights to a public ridge of response-style variance measured across fixed probes; a clone sharing weights lands on the same ridge, so duplication becomes visible as an anomalous cluster. Each identity must anchor a fresh random seed whose probe responses are logged, and matching ridge coordinates across two accounts flags them as one lineage. The fable of independent origins collapses because an attacker must retrain per identity, paying full compute plus a monthly probe audit fee, roughly the cost of a new model each time.
